title: רב שמואל בר יהודה הנדוואה

paragraphs:
Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah the Indian; see his entry. In the first chapter of Kiddushin, 22, end of side b: he and his father converted. Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah stood before Rav Yehudah, who said to him, “Go up and join the five for halitzah ….” He answered, “We learned: in a court of Israelites, not in a court of gentiles; and I am a convert.” Rashi explains: he and his father converted, and I am disqualified for halitzah. Rav Yehudah said, “On the word of someone such as Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah, I would impair a document's standing”: Mitzvat Halitzah, 101, end of side b. Tosafot there, in Ba Siman 49b, and Sanhedrin 36, end of side b, write: Rabbenu Tam regularly explains that the Shmuel bar Yehudah in Mitzvat Halitzah is the son of R' Yehudah the Indian. This is not so, for R' Shmuel bar Yehudah's mother was an Israelite. See Tosafot Yeshanim, Ketubbot 44b. His mother made him a silver scraper for Shabbat: Shabbat 147b. Rashi, Bekhorot 37, beginning of side b, writes that he is mentioned in many places in the language of a tannaitic teaching, “Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah taught”: Ein Ma'amidin and Shabbat 79a.

He said in R' Abba bar Zavda's name. He said in R' Abba's name, who said in Rav Huna's name: Shabbat 5, beginning of side a, 98a. Abaye said to him: Menahot 42b; Gittin 16b. In the editions designated בשס״ח [provisionally the new Talmud editions; not independently collated], it should read “R' Ammi said to him.” I suspect that it was corrected thus for the reason I write immediately below concerning Rava. In R' Elazar's name: Kirah, 38b. And Rav Dimi. He said in R' Hanina's name: Shabbat 52a. He said to Rav Yehudah, “Sharp one”: Ketubbot 12b; see above. Rav Yehudah permitted treating the eye with kohl on Shabbat. R' Shmuel bar Yehudah said to him, “Whoever listens to Yehudah desecrates Shabbat.” Eventually his own eyes hurt, and he sent to him: “Is it permitted or forbidden?” He sent back, “For everyone it is permitted; for you it is forbidden”: Avodah Zarah 28b.

He said in R' Yohanan's name: Shabbat 37b; Gittin 16a. “When R' Shmuel bar Yehudah came, he said in R' Yohanan's name”: Yevamot 55, end of side b; Gittin 23b, 40, 41; Sanhedrin 31b; Avodah Zarah 54b. Rav Yosef said, “How excellent is this teaching that R' Shmuel bar Yehudah said they state in the West”: Berakhot 14b. He said, “Do I not know that Rav Yosef said in Rav Yehudah's name, in Shmuel's name …?”: Shabbat 37b. Ulla came to his house: Shabbat 109b. He taught before Rava: Yoma 11b. This requires examination, for the foregoing suggests that he was Rav Yehudah's colleague. How could he teach before him as a pupil, when Rava was the pupil of Rav Yosef, Rav Yehudah's pupil, and Rava was born when Rav Yehudah died? Perhaps it should read: he taught before Rabbah.
